title: Regime Shifts, Populism, and 2025 Predictions - Systematic Investor 323

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/Regime Shifts, Populism, and 2025 Predictions - Systematic Investor 323.docx

speakers: Jim Carson (guest co-host, Chicago derivatives/vol strategist; name as transcribed)
summary: Systematic Investor 323 (Dec 2024): regime shift and populism, option-dealer vol compression and dispersion, election-year equity seasonality, gold calls and Bitcoin.

coverage.note: intro, small talk; regime change non-linear
regime view; post-election trend followers; Ukraine/geopolitics
index returns; VIX futures vs ETP; vol-correlation mechanism
2017 vol/correlation outlier; alpha non-directional; post-event vol compression
VIX vs surface; where rotation occurs; Nvidia
Trump/COVID, cycle analogue, real vs nominal

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: we're broadly in a very different environment than we have been the last 40 years
claims.claim: The world has moved into a different regime from the last 40 years, and the shift is non-linear: slow for a long time and then sudden.

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: this is a calm before a bigger storm
claims.claim: Markets are in a calm before an acceleration into a broader regime change (not necessarily a crash).

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the US election has in large part been in line with the overall exposures of trend followers in the aftermath of the election, long equities
claims.claim: After the Nov 2024 US election trend followers were positioned long equities and the dollar and out of long bonds, which paid; long precious metals hurt.
claims.direction: long equities, long USD; avoid long bonds

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: perhaps an even better sector for trend followers so far in November has been soft commodities, like coffee, like cocoa
claims.claim: Soft commodities (coffee, cocoa, each up about 20% in November 2024) were a top trend sector, showing the value of broad diversification.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: My own trend barometer stood at 41 last night, that's a neutral reading.
claims.claim: Trend barometer at 41 is a neutral reading while longer-term strategies were doing somewhat better than the reading suggested.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the support for Ukraine can, you know, go away very quickly. And and I just don't think Europe is is ready
claims.claim: A new Trump administration could quickly end US support for Ukraine, which Europe is not prepared for.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: up about 2%, and just slightly positive for the year now.
claims.claim: In Nov 2024 SocGen Trend was about +2% (slightly positive YTD) vs S&P 500 +25.6% YTD, so trend lagged equities.

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: VIX futures are more efficient. They're also more capital efficient.
claims.claim: For a multi-million VIX trade, use VIX futures rather than ETPs like VXX: ETPs add market-maker edge and rebalancing costs, futures are margined and more capital efficient when rates are 5%.
claims.conditions: higher rates raise cost of unmargined capital

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: how correlation of constituents and stocks in the market are tied to volatility
claims.claim: When index volatility is compressed (dealers long options), the index is pinned and idiosyncratic moves must be offset elsewhere, so single-stock volatility rises and constituent correlation falls.
claims.indicator: index implied vol vs constituent correlation / dispersion
claims.direction: long dispersion when index vol is pinned
claims.testable: yes - implied vs realised correlation data

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: We had 30% lower implied and realized volatility than any other time in history.
claims.claim: In 2017 implied and realised volatility were 30% below any other time in 120 years and constituent correlation was 25% below any other time, evidence that vol compression and correlation breakdown are linked.

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: most of the edges truly true alpha it's generally not directional, right? It's generally market structure dynamics
claims.claim: Real alpha is mostly non-directional and comes from market-structure dynamics such as option dealer positioning and dispersion.

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: you have now been delivered longer vol at a much lower level. And that brings the whole curve down
claims.claim: After an event (election) passes, dealers end up long vol at lower levels, selling pressure compresses realised then implied vol until a rally to low vol triggers call and put buy-backs.
claims.indicator: vol supply, dealer positioning, implied vol curve
claims.conditions: post-event vol collapse; resolves with rally then vol buying

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: These next this next month and a half to two months really call it two months cuz it's really through early January
claims.claim: Year-end flows (Thanksgiving, Christmas, bond and charm flows from skew, structural products, releveraging) push the market higher and compress short-dated vol through early January, driving dispersion and rotation.
claims.direction: long equities, short short-dated vol into early January

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: 100% vol compression into rallies is leading to correlation breakdown, which is also by definition hurting breath
claims.claim: Vol compression during rallies breaks correlation and so narrows market breadth, in addition to passive flows.

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: the way we take advantage of it is we watch very closely what's happening in the vol markets, right? That vol supply is the key
claims.claim: The way to exploit the compression/dispersion dynamic is to track vol supply (dealer positioning) in the options market.

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: The VIX is not what you should be looking at to understand fully.
claims.claim: VIX is not a pure view of vol because of skew: when the market falls VIX pops while underlying vol often falls, so watch price of underlying options and fixed-strike vol across the surface instead.
claims.indicator: fixed-strike implied vol surface vs VIX

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: one good place to look is shortfall areas in the market because the long ball market areas of the market are likely to stay pinned
claims.claim: Rotation and correlation breakdown happen in areas where vol is short-supplied (Nvidia, and since July 2024 the Russell with heavy upside call buying), while well-supplied areas stay pinned.

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: It's had incredible momentum and that momentum is slowing.
claims.claim: Nvidia momentum was slowing with good-but-not-great earnings and accounting worries, a possible laggard.

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: America First policy and you know, things that [L260] largely are more likely to to benefit uh kind of smaller cap domestic stocks
claims.claim: America First policy favours small-cap domestic stocks, so Russell outperforms while the S&P grinds higher and Nvidia lags.
claims.direction: long Russell / small caps vs Nvidia

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: meme names, you know, have a have a tailwind in the form of the new pump and dump
claims.claim: Narrative and meme stocks get a tailwind from Musk's reach plus Trump's bully pulpit, with rotation into narrative names.

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: They they lower out the long-term rates. Guess what? It's stimulus
claims.claim: Reflexivity: the Fed's rate-cut talk lowers long rates, which is stimulus (sequestered housing demand released), making inflation and growth stickier than expected.

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: after a big run at the end of the year you have to be cautious
claims.claim: After a big year-end run, early January is a window to be cautious, particularly after up years and in election years.

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: there's a one and a half to two week window here where you got to start seeing something
claims.claim: Tailored trades use short time windows: if the expected decline does not show in 1.5-2 weeks, drop the trade.

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: mid-February we said you got to go long. You got to go aggressively long
claims.claim: Went aggressively long from mid-Feb 2024 on election-year, vol-compression and Fed-flow grounds and held until August.

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: It's good time to sell short-dated vol, buy long-dated vol
claims.claim: In vol-compression grinds, sell short-dated vol and buy long-dated vol, collecting the grind while owning protection.
claims.direction: short short-dated vol / long long-dated vol
claims.conditions: when dealers are long gamma and market grinds up

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: when it breaks it breaks spectacularly. By the way, that 2017 period we talked about it broke with the volpocalypse
claims.claim: Compressed-vol regimes end suddenly and violently (volpocalypse), so stay aware and buy convexity.

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: We targeted likely September. It happened in August. It happened early.
claims.claim: The forecast 10% vol event came in August rather than September, showing timing precision is limited.

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: The end of the year is going to be a massive rally and that we should hit 6,000 to 6,200 end of year
claims.claim: Forecast S&P 500 at 6,000-6,200 by year end 2024 and mid-January, followed by a period to hedge.
claims.direction: long into year end, hedge mid-January

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: if you take those out of the data set, the number for the 100 years of of history is actually 5%.
claims.claim: Election-year S&P returns average 11% over 100 years, but five years (1964, 68, 72, 76, 80) averaging 21.5% drive it; excluding them it is about 5%.

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: The market went nowhere for 14 years and lost 70% of its value in real terms.
claims.claim: From 1968 to 1982 the market went nowhere (-70% real) yet every election year was up double digits.

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: feeding money through Federal Reserve policy, and they're pumping the market to get elected
claims.claim: In populist periods, policymakers pump markets before elections via Fed policy and pay the bill in non-election years.
claims.direction: long in election years, cautious in other years

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: The last one was 21%. And this one, we're now at 25%
claims.claim: The last two populist-era election years were +21% and about +25%, consistent with the pattern.

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: many, many times, most
claims.claim: Be cautious from January but not before, since the best returns often come at the end of a run.

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: I would focus on a a January 13th to 15th window. Um, as being your first shot.
claims.claim: First shot for a hedge or top is January 13-15, 2025, then February (expiry) if it does not occur, using convexity.
claims.conditions: after blow-off top and unpinning of dealer wall

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: We continue to rally despite knowing about COVID into Feb OPEX
claims.claim: COVID analogy: markets rallied into Feb OPEX then fell over 30% from Feb to March; March quarterly OPEX adds stress potential.

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: you need something idiosyncratic to happen to unleash what is a secular trend
claims.claim: Populist cycles need a catalyst (Kennedy assassination in 1963, COVID in 2020) to unleash fiscal expansion and inflation.

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: the political winds have shifted as a function of demographics
claims.claim: Demographics (older capital owners vs younger labour) shift politics towards populism as the disadvantaged young gain dominance, over multiple election cycles from 2009 Tea Party/Occupy.

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: And that paired with a catalyst which was COVID
claims.claim: Trump moved the right to the left; COVID released massive fiscal spending that sets up 10-20 years of populist policy.

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: there's 18 years in there 64 to 82. Um this probably goes to 2038 or so.
claims.claim: Treating 2020 as the analogue of 1964, the populist cycle (1964-82 length) would run to about 2038.

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: we had populist periods before the '60s and '70s and they weren't inflationary
claims.claim: Populist periods can be deflationary (Great Depression) yet in real terms markets show the same pattern; inflation and rates drive nominal outcomes.

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: the reason we're more likely to be inflationary as opposed to something like the Great Depression is because of the Federal Reserve
claims.claim: Because the modern Fed will use inflation to avoid depression, the current populist period is more likely inflationary than deflationary.

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: they have a dual mandate. They have one tool.
claims.claim: The Fed has two mandates and one tool and structural inflation from borrowing against the future, so its put is less reliable and volatility will rise.

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: historically the greatest volatility during these populist periods does not come in equity markets
claims.claim: In populist periods the biggest volatility is in FX, bond yields and precious metals, not in equities or energy.
claims.direction: buy vol / convexity in FX, rates, gold

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: this is a massive structural secular opportunity
claims.claim: In 2021-22 long-dated gold options/upside call vol were cheap while oil vol was high; gold call skew later exploded.
claims.conditions: when gold vol is low and unloved

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: the best performing asset from the '68 to '82 period, not even close, is gold. But it was also the most volatile asset.
claims.claim: Gold was the best asset in 1968-82 but suffered 50% drawdowns, so own long-dated calls rather than the underlying and expect big swings.

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: expect when you start hearing people turn negative on it, that's when you start buying it with two hands again
claims.claim: Gold volatility is greatest when everyone is on one side; buy when sentiment turns negative.
claims.direction: buy gold after sentiment turns negative

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: Bitcoin has captured the belief of this these generations.
claims.claim: Bitcoin captures the belief of younger generations rising to political power and may cap some of gold's upside; regulatory risk is the main headwind and Trump's win removes the largest overhang for 4 years.
claims.conditions: until sovereigns see it as a threat to dollar privilege

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: at the same time that we are amidst this populous period that it is popular to gut government. I think that's probably not going to end well
claims.claim: Gutting government in a populist period is contradictory; the 2017 tax cuts gave 95% of benefit to corporations and the wealthy, which exacerbates populism.

claims.speaker: Jim Carson
claims.quote: my guess is it'll extend the populist cycle a bit
claims.claim: A dual approach (populist tariffs and immigration plus deregulation/cuts) likely extends the populist cycle and prolongs poor equity returns in real terms.
